summary.text: Hal Rafter is a Democratic candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Rockingham 1, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
He previously represented the district in the House from October 2023 to December 2024.

paragraphs.text: Hal Rafter was born in Mason, New Hampshire, and earned a master's degree from the University of New Hampshire in 1978.
His career experience includes working as a senior programmer, a housing analyst and an adjunct professor.

Rafter ran for Rockingham 32 in 2020 and lost the general election to incumbent Terry Roy, and he was among the Democrats who advanced from the 2022 Rockingham 1 primary but did not win in the general election.
He won the September 19, 2023 special general election for Rockingham 1, defeating James Guzofski, and assumed office on October 4, 2023.
He left office on December 4, 2024, after the November 2024 general election, in which Republicans Scott Bryer, James Guzofski and Paul Tudor won the three seats.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, Rafter said he had lived in Nottingham for 38 years, served eight years on the school board and three as a selectman, and that he and his wife had run small businesses.
In that survey he named public education, defending rights, and addressing climate change among his priorities.
